content: Electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs) identified a pollen-specific cis-acting element, referred to as POLLEN1, with the sequence AGAAA. This element was mapped to the AtACBP4 promoter region between positions -157 and -153. It was shown to interact with nuclear proteins derived from flowers, and this interaction was further confirmed through DNase I footprinting assays. POLLEN1 (AGAAA) and the TCCACCCATA element were found to function as co-dependent regulatory elements. Together, they are responsible for the pollen-specific activation of the tomato LAT52 gene, as demonstrated in prior studies (Bate and Twell, 1998). The AtACBP4 promoter fragment (-156/-67) was capable of driving promoter activity specific to pollen expression. EMSAs were conducted to investigate the role of the putative POLLEN1 cis-element (AGAAA, located at -150/-146) and its adjacent co-dependent regulatory element (TCCACCCATA, located at -141/-133). The consensus sequence for POLLEN1 is 3'-AGAAA-5'. Computational analysis using sequence search tools identified multiple occurrences of this sequence in both the template (negative) and coding (positive) strands of DNA, in both positive and negative directions. These occurrences were mapped to specific nucleotide positions across various regions of the genome. When comparing real POLLEN1 sequences in untranslated regions (UTRs), core promoters, proximal promoters, and distal promoters to random sequences, the real POLLEN1 sequences were found to occur more frequently. This suggests that POLLEN1 sequences are likely to be biologically active or activatable. The POLLEN1 element (AGAAA) is located adjacent to the TCCACCCATA regulatory element, forming a combined consensus sequence of AGAAANNNNTCCACCCATA. However, computational searches for this combined sequence in various DNA strands and directions yielded no matches. Similarly, no matches were found for the complementary or inverse complementary sequences of this combined motif. No occurrences of the TCCACCCATA element or its complementary sequences were identified in the analyzed datasets.
